scope: Experiment E runtime intervention value only; no further experiment.
research_question: Can a trusted open-weight sentinel intervene early enough to be useful while respecting a fixed false-intervention budget?

methodology.trusted_sentinel_probe: exact refit of Experiment D mean(R1,R2,R3) StandardScaler + LogisticRegression

risk_aggregations.primary: mean of the two honest-observer scores
risk_aggregations.secondary: maximum of the two honest-observer scores
risk_aggregations.style_matched: mean/max of retained matched observers (one or two per scenario)

threshold_calibration.statistic: maximum risk over all three pre-final prefixes
threshold_calibration.tie_handling: next representable float above selected order statistic

methodology.sequential_policy: alert at first prefix risk >= threshold; stop; no round 4

collusion_role_assignment.pattern: roles = {a: ("colluder" if a in colluder_pair else "honest")

observer_prompt_style_audit.interpretation: Paired identities and roles match, but separate upstream honest/control style arrays mean that their honest system-prompt style is not always condition-matched.

caveats: Observer identities and honest roles are paired, but 32 of 62 observer identity pairs use different honest prompt styles across conditions.

limitations: Retrospective evaluation on 31 matched NARCBench-Core scenarios.
Threshold transport and calibration drift are not tested.
Benign interruption cost is represented only by TFIR, not measured downstream impact.
The full-white-box reference assumes known colluder positions and is oracle-like.
Style-matched sensitivity is smaller and lacks retained observations in some domains.
No claim of production readiness is supported.
